critical_code_review_comments: content_lock.sync_overview() unconditionally rewrites apps.name from navbar brand on every save. Explicitly requested per spec, but the side effect is that PATCH /api/apps/{id} {name:...} silently loses if the caller doesn't also update the navbar brand — worth surfacing in Overview UI copy (e.g. 'Renaming here updates the Navbar too') so admins aren't surprised.

content_lock.sync_overview() reads the first non-'/' page as home only after sorting by slug != '/'; if a tenant has no page with slug '/' the first page in the list is treated as home. Fine today (seed always adds '/'), but a defensive `if home['slug'] != '/': return None` (or explicit search) would make the intent obvious.

sync_overview thumbnail selector iterates all blocks and picks the first prop key in ('image','bg','background'). Order of dict iteration is insertion-order in Python 3.7+, but block prop key order isn't guaranteed across builders — consider preferring the hero block's image/bg first, else fall back, to keep the thumbnail visually stable.

site_snapshot.updated_at is written on every save even when nothing else in the snapshot changed (e.g. theme save with identical theme). That's the intended freshness signal, but the frontend 8s poll compares by value not timestamp, so nothing user-visible flickers — acceptable.

Startup runs sync_all_overviews sequentially; with 7 tenants it's instant, but at 100+ tenants this becomes a 1–2s serial IO stall. Fire-and-forget via asyncio.gather bounded to N would be safer as the platform grows.

resync_overview endpoint returns 400 with detail 'This tenant has no Site Mode pages yet' — correct. Consider also 200 with an empty snapshot for idempotency, so the UI can call it right after creating a tenant without a try/except.
